mainTopic: How a returned קומץ avoids being sanctified by a כלי שרת, and whether a קומץ may be taken from a vessel resting on the ground
overview: The amud opens with a קשיא: when the כהן puts the קומץ back into the vessel holding the מנחה, that כלי שרת should sanctify it and make it פסול. רבי יוחנן answers that כלי שרת sanctify only with intent (מדעת). The גמרא then explains that vessels do not sanctify פסולין to be offered, but they do sanctify them so that they become disqualified. רב עמרם gives a different answer: the קומץ was put back on top of the flour and never entered the vessel. After two more rounds, his case becomes a level-full bowl where the handful slides into the dent by itself, as if a monkey put it there. רבי ירמיה asks why the גמרא did not simply say the vessel was on the ground. This opens the question of whether a קומץ may be taken from a vessel resting on the ground. רבי זירא tells the story of אבימי, who always answered רב נחמן that another כהן lifts the vessel, and he defends that answer against a משנה. Finally the question is put to רב ששת, who points to how the לחם הפנים and its bowls are changed on שבת, and his proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Putting the handful back should sanctify it and disqualify it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge: when the קומץ is returned to its original vessel, that vessel should sanctify it, and so it should become פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he puts the handful back in its place, it should become sanctified and become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge from the earlier discussion. Its point is that putting the קומץ back into the vessel of the מנחה should count as sanctifying it in a כלי שרת, which would make it פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original vessel holding the מנחה is also a כלי שרת. So the challenge asks why it should matter which vessel the קומץ is placed in. Any כלי שרת should sanctify it, and that sanctity would bring on the disqualification.

keyTerms.meaning: The handful of flour the כהן takes from a מנחה to burn on the מזבח
To its place, here meaning back into the vessel it came from
To become sanctified by a כלי שרת

phrases.english: And when he returns the handful to its place,
it should become sanctified and become disqualified.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the word in square brackets. Both mean "it should become sanctified."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that returning the קומץ to its original vessel does not sanctify or disqualify it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The original vessel is also a כלי שרת. Any כלי שרת should sanctify what is placed in it, so the קומץ should become sanctified and therefore disqualified.

steps.title: Service vessels sanctify only with intent
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that כלי שרת sanctify only items placed in them with intent, so putting the קומץ back does not sanctify it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This teaches that כלי שרת sanctify only with intent.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. A כלי שרת sanctifies something only when it is placed there on purpose so that the vessel will sanctify it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהן who puts the קומץ back into the מנחה's vessel has no plan to sanctify it there. Without that intent, the vessel does nothing to the קומץ. So the קומץ does not become sanctified, and it does not become פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: This teaches, this shows us (drawing a rule from a case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general rule about how כלי שרת work: sanctification by a כלי depends on the person's intent.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said: That is to say:
service vessels do not sanctify
except with intent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a condition (intent) that is required for the rule to apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any item placed in a כלי שרת becomes sanctified
steps.terutzMaskana: A כלי שרת sanctifies only what is placed in it with intent, so the returned קומץ is not affected

steps.title: Challenge from ריש לקיש's question about disqualified items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that with intent, vessels do sanctify. It then cites רבי יוחנן's own ruling that כלי שרת do not sanctify פסולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean that with intent they sanctify? But ריש לקיש asked רבי יוחנן whether כלי שרת sanctify disqualified items so that they may be offered from the start, and he answered: they do not sanctify!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. Here רבי יוחנן seems to say that vessels sanctify with intent, yet elsewhere he told ריש לקיש that vessels do not sanctify disqualified items at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference is that a כלי שרת can sanctify when intent is present. But רבי יוחנן's answer to ריש לקיש, "they do not sanctify," sounds like a flat rule for פסולין. That seems to contradict the idea that vessels sanctify, and so make פסול, items like the קומץ.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (posed a question to him)
From the start, as the proper first choice
To be offered on the מזבח

phrases.english: This implies that with intent they sanctify?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Reish Lakish ask Rabbi Yoḥanan:
service vessels, what is the law, do they sanctify
disqualified items to be offered from the outset?
And he said to him: They do not sanctify!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדַּעַת מְקַדְּשִׁין? וְהָא בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ מֵרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 2
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that כלי שרת sanctify with intent
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן also told ריש לקיש that כלי שרת do not sanctify disqualified items. That seems to clash with the idea that they sanctify, and thereby disqualify, items placed in them with intent.

steps.title: They do not sanctify to be offered, but they do sanctify to become disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן's answer was limited: vessels do not sanctify פסולין so that they may be offered, but they do sanctify them so that they become disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told him: They do not sanctify them to be offered, but they do sanctify them to become disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by clarifying what רבי יוחנן really told ריש לקיש. He only meant that a vessel cannot make a disqualified item fit for the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי שרת's sanctity cannot fix a פסול item. It does give the item a status of sanctity, though, and that status means the item becomes formally disqualified. So the two statements of רבי יוחנן fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not sanctify an item to make it fit to be offered
They do sanctify an item, with the result that it becomes disqualified

steps.confusionAlert: "Sanctifying" here does not make the item fit to be offered. Here it means the opposite: the item gets a holy status, and that status is what makes it פסול.

phrases.english: He said to him: They do not sanctify to be offered,
but they do sanctify to become disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֵין מְקַדְּשִׁין לִיקְרַב, אֲבָל מִקַּדְּשִׁין לִיפָּסֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the cited statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן said that vessels do not sanctify disqualified items in any way
steps.terutzMaskana: Vessels do not make disqualified items fit to be offered, but they do sanctify them so that they become disqualified

steps.title: רב עמרם: the handful was put on top of a heaped bowl
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם gives a different answer to the first challenge: the קומץ was returned onto a heaped bowl, so it never entered the vessel itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said: For example, where he returned it to a heaped bowl.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם offers a second answer to the challenge from step 1, without needing the rule about intent. The קומץ was placed on top of a pile of flour that rose above the rim of the bowl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if a כלי שרת sanctifies without intent, it can only sanctify what is inside it. A קומץ resting on a heap above the bowl never entered the space inside the vessel, so it is not sanctified and does not become פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as in a case where

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to why the returned קומץ is not sanctified. רבי יוחנן says a כלי שרת sanctifies only with intent. רב עמרם says the קומץ sat on a heaped bowl and never entered the vessel.

phrases.english: Rav Amram said:
Such as where he returned it to a heaped bowl.
phrases.notes: The flour was piled above the rim, so the קומץ rested on top and never went inside the bowl itself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶחְזִירוֹ לְבִיסָא גְּדוּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the challenge in step 1 and offers a different answer from רבי יוחנן's
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case so the challenge does not apply
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The returned קומץ went inside the vessel and should be sanctified
steps.terutzMaskana: The קומץ rested on a heap above the bowl's rim, outside the vessel, so it was not sanctified

steps.title: How could he take a handful from a heaped bowl?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב עמרם: if the מנחה was heaped above the rim, the original handful was not taken from inside the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how did he take the handful in the first place?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב עמרם's answer from Step 5. If the flour was piled above the rim, the first handful came from outside the vessel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קמיצה must be taken from flour that is inside a כלי שרת. With a heaped bowl, the top part sticks out above the vessel. So the original קמיצה would have been done wrongly. The same feature that solved the returning problem now breaks the taking of the handful.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking the handful from the מנחה
The handful of flour that is burned on the מזבח

phrases.english: And taking the handful, how did he take it?
phrases.notes: The handful must be taken from inside the vessel, but the top of a heaped pile is above the vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב עמרם's heaped-bowl answer
steps.kashyaTarget: רב עמרם's case of a heaped bowl
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the flour is above the vessel, the original קמיצה was not done from within a כלי שרת, so the קמיצה itself would be invalid.

steps.title: The bowl was filled exactly to the brim
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adjusts the case: the bowl was full to the brim but not heaped.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the case is where he returned it to a bowl filled to the brim.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא changes the case to a bowl filled exactly level with the rim. This way, both moves can work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the flour is level with the rim, the handful is taken from flour that is inside the vessel. When the handful is put back on top, it sits above the rim, outside the vessel's space. So the vessel does not sanctify it.

keyTerms.meaning: A bowl filled exactly to the brim, not heaped

phrases.english: Rather, such as where he returned it
to a full bowl.
phrases.notes: Full meaning level with the rim, not piled up. The returned handful rests above the vessel's opening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by refining רב עמרם's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bowl was heaped, so the קמיצה would have been taken from outside the vessel
steps.terutzMaskana: The bowl was level-full. The handful is taken from inside, and it is returned above the rim.

steps.title: Taking the handful leaves a dent inside the vessel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that taking the handful leaves a hollow, so returning it puts it back inside the vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: But once he took the handful, he made a dent. So when he puts it back, he is putting it back inside the vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the level-bowl answer. Taking a handful leaves a hole below the rim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the קמיצה, the surface is no longer level. There is a dent below the rim. Putting the handful back fills that dent, which is inside the vessel, so the vessel should sanctify it again.

phrases.english: But once he took the handful,
he made a dent,
so when he returns it, into the vessel
he is returning it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵיוָן דִּקְמַץ לֵיהּ עֲבַד לֵיהּ גּוּמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the level-bowl answer of Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the returned handful stays above the vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קמיצה creates a dent below the rim, so the handful goes back into the vessel's space and should be sanctified.

steps.title: The handful slides back in by itself
steps.stepSummary: The כהן sets the handful on the vessel's wall and shakes the vessel, so it falls in on its own, as if a monkey put it there.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he returns it, he lays it on the wall of the vessel and shakes it, and it falls in by itself. It is as if a monkey returned it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the כהן does not put the handful into the dent himself. It slides in on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is still רב עמרם's approach, which works even if vessels sanctify without intent. Even so, a vessel sanctifies only what a person places in it. Here the handful drops in from the shaking, as if an animal had done it, so it is not sanctified.

keyTerms.meaning: The wall or side of a vessel

phrases.english: When he returns it,
he places it on the wall of the vessel,
and shakes it, and it falls by itself,
so it is as though a monkey returned it.
phrases.notes: A monkey isn't a person, so the handful counts as getting there without a person placing it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכִּי מַהְדַּר לֵיהּ, מַנַּח לֵיהּ אַדֻּפְנָא דְּמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Describing a method that avoids human placement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Returning the handful into the dent puts it inside the vessel, so it is sanctified
steps.terutzMaskana: It falls in by itself, so no person placed it, and it is not sanctified.
steps.whatToRemember: The final picture: the bowl is level-full, and the handful slides back into the dent by itself, like a monkey put it there. So the vessel does not sanctify it.

steps.title: Why not use a vessel resting on the ground?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא why the case was not simply explained as a vessel resting on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said to רבי זירא: Let us explain it as a case where he returned it to a vessel resting on the ground!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה suggests an easier way out of the whole problem of returning the handful. He asks: why not say the vessel was sitting on the floor?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a vessel resting on the ground does not sanctify, that would be a simple way to explain why the returned handful stays valid. Then there would be no need for heaped bowls, level bowls or monkeys. The fact that the גמרא went to so much trouble needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: A vessel resting on the ground rather than held
Let us explain it as (a suggestion for a different case)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה לְרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said to Rabbi Zeira:
And let us explain it as where he returned it
to a vessel resting on the ground!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ כְּגוֹן שֶׁהֶחְזִירוֹ לִכְלִי הַמּוּנָּח עַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the earlier answers did not use a simpler case
steps.kashyaTarget: The complicated case setups in Steps 5–9
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel on the ground would be a simpler way to avoid sanctification, if such a vessel does not sanctify.

steps.title: Can a קומץ be taken from a vessel on the ground?
steps.stepSummary: Since the simpler case was not used, רבי ירמיה asks whether a vessel on the ground does sanctify, so that one may take a קומץ from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, should we learn from this that one may take a handful from a vessel resting on the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה draws a possible conclusion from the fact that the ground-vessel case was not used. He asks whether that conclusion is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not using the easy case suggests that a vessel on the ground does sanctify what is put in it. If so, it is a proper כלי שרת even while on the ground. Then the קמיצה could be done from it.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this
that one may take a handful from a vessel on the ground?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ קוֹמְצִין מִכְּלִי שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the case not chosen in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a vessel resting on the ground sanctifies, and so whether קמיצה may be done from it

steps.title: This was an open question in רב חסדא's study hall
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that this exact question was raised when רבי אבימי learned מנחות in רב חסדא's study hall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You have touched on a question that was asked before us, when רבי אבימי was learning מנחות in רב חסדא's study hall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא does not settle the question. He says it was already a known open question from earlier learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא confirms that the issue is real and was debated before. He places it in the setting where רבי אבימי studied מסכת מנחות at רב חסדא's study hall. This mention of where אבימי learned will itself be questioned next.

keyTerms.meaning: The study hall of a teacher

phrases.english: He said to him:
You have touched on a question that was asked before us,
when Rabbi Avimi was learning Menachot
in the study hall of Rav Chisda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רבי ירמיה's question in Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question was already raised in רב חסדא's study hall. The full discussion follows later.

steps.title: Wasn't אבימי רב חסדא's teacher?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to ask how אבימי could have learned at רב חסדא's study hall, since רב חסדא himself said he took blows from אבימי while learning from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did אבימי really learn in רב חסדא's study hall? But רב חסדא said: I took many blows from אבימי over this teaching. If the court announces a sale on consecutive days, it is for thirty days. If it announces on Monday, Thursday and Monday, it is for sixty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts with a side question about who was the teacher and who was the student. The answer comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא describes אבימי correcting him harshly about a law of court announcements. That makes אבימי sound like רב חסדא's teacher. Then it is strange to say אבימי learned at רב חסדא's study hall.
steps.confusionAlert: This is a side question about who taught whom. It does not answer the question about a vessel on the ground; that discussion picks up again in step 17.

phrases.english: And did Avimi learn in Rav Chisda's study hall?
But didn't Rav Chisda say:
I absorbed many blows from Avimi
phrases.notes: He means Avimi corrected him sharply, the way a teacher corrects a student.

phrases.english: over this teaching:
if it comes to announce on consecutive days, thirty days;
Monday, Thursday and Monday, sixty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲבִימִי בֵּי רַב חִסְדָּא תָּנֵי? וְהָאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions a detail mentioned in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that אבימי learned in רב חסדא's study hall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב חסדא describes taking corrections from אבימי, which shows אבימי was his teacher, not his student.

steps.title: אבימי forgot the tractate and went to his student to relearn it
steps.stepSummary: אבימי was really the teacher, but he forgot מסכת מנחות, so he came to his student רב חסדא to relearn it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבימי forgot the tractate, and he came to רב חסדא to help him remember what he had learned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. אבימי was the teacher, but he had forgotten מנחות and came to his own student to review it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both statements are true. רב חסדא learned from אבימי and took blows from him as a student. Later, אבימי came to רב חסדא's study hall only to get back what he had forgotten.

keyTerms.meaning: A tractate of the תלמוד (here, מנחות)
Was uprooted, meaning it was forgotten

phrases.english: Avimi, the tractate
was uprooted for him,
phrases.notes: In other words, he forgot it. Some versions have the word in round brackets instead; it means the same thing.

phrases.english: and he came before Rav Chisda
to recall his learning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the circumstances: the teacher came to the student only to review
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning in רב חסדא's study hall meant אבימי was רב חסדא's student
steps.terutzMaskana: אבימי was the teacher and came only to recover what he had forgotten

steps.title: Why didn't אבימי call his student to come to him
steps.stepSummary: If רב חסדא was the student, אבימי should have sent for him rather than going to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him send for him, and let him come to him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. A teacher normally calls his student to him, so why did אבימי travel?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Honoring a teacher means the student comes to the teacher. אבימי going to רב חסדא seems backward.

phrases.english: But let him send for him
and let him come to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of step 14
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אבימי came to רב חסדא's study hall
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teacher would have his student come to him, not travel to the student

steps.title: Going himself would help him remember better
steps.stepSummary: אבימי thought that putting in the effort to travel would make his learning succeed more.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: this way the matter will be more successful.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that אבימי chose to go to his student on purpose, because the effort would help him remember.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trip was not about who is greater. Working hard for learning helps it stay with a person, so אבימי picked the harder path.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter succeeds, it is helped along

steps.whatToRemember: אבימי was רב חסדא's teacher. He forgot מנחות and chose to travel to his student to relearn it, because effort helps learning last.

phrases.english: He thought: this way
the matter will be more successful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a reason for the unusual behavior
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The student should have come to the teacher
steps.terutzMaskana: אבימי went himself on purpose so that he would remember better

steps.title: רב נחמן asks Avimi how one takes a handful
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן met אבימי and asked him how one takes the קומץ from a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן met him and said to him: How does one take a קומץ?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the story behind רבי זירא's answer from step 12. רב נחמן meets אבימי and asks him a practical question about the קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the real point of the story. The question is about the physical way the קומץ is taken, and it leads to the issue of a vessel resting on the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: He met him, he came across him
One takes a קומץ, the handful taken from a מנחה

phrases.english: Rav Nachman met him,
he said to him: How does one take a handful?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּגַע בֵּיהּ רַב נַחְמָן אֲמַר לֵיהּ כֵּיצַד קוֹמְצִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story רבי זירא mentioned in step 12, after the side question of steps 13-16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The proper way to take a קומץ from a מנחה

steps.title: אבימי points to a vessel: from this one
steps.stepSummary: אבימי answered by pointing to a vessel and saying the קומץ is taken from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: From this vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי answers by pointing to a vessel, which the next step shows was resting on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His answer seems to suggest that one may take a קומץ from a vessel sitting on the ground. That is exactly what רב נחמן challenges next.

phrases.english: He said to him: From this vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קומץ is taken from this vessel, which was on the ground

steps.title: Can one take a handful from a vessel on the ground
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that a קומץ may not be taken from a vessel resting on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But does one take a קומץ from a vessel that is on the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges אבימי's answer. The vessel was sitting on the ground, and he assumes that is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words וכי show that רב נחמן takes it for granted that a vessel on the ground cannot be used. This is the same question רבי ירמיה asked in step 11.

phrases.english: He said to him: But does one take a handful
from a vessel that is on the ground?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי קוֹמְצִין מִכְּלִי שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 18
steps.kashyaTarget: אבימי's pointing to a vessel on the ground
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel on the ground seems unfit for taking the קומץ

steps.title: A כהן lifts the vessel first
steps.stepSummary: אבימי explains that he meant a כהן lifts the vessel off the ground, and then the קומץ is taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A כהן lifts it.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי clarifies his answer. The vessel will not stay on the ground, because a כהן picks it up first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבימי does not argue that a vessel on the ground is fine. He changes the case so that the vessel is held up when the קומץ is taken. The question about a vessel on the ground is still left open.

phrases.english: He said to him: That a priest lifts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the case: the vessel is lifted first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אבימי meant the קומץ is taken while the vessel sits on the ground
steps.terutzMaskana: Another כהן lifts the vessel, so it is not on the ground

steps.title: How are the meal offerings sanctified
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks a second question: how is a מנחה sanctified in a vessel?
steps.simpleTranslation: How does one sanctify the מנחות?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן asks a new question, this time about placing the מנחה in a vessel to make it holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting the flour into a holy vessel is the step that sanctifies it. The same issue about a vessel on the ground will come up again.

keyTerms.meaning: Sanctify, make holy (by placing in a holy vessel)

phrases.english: How does one sanctify the meal offerings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question, parallel to step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The proper way to sanctify a מנחה in a vessel

steps.title: אבימי says: one places it into this vessel
steps.stepSummary: אבימי again points to a vessel on the ground and says the מנחה is placed into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He places it into this vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי answers the same way as before, pointing to a vessel that is on the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the issue is not taking out the קומץ but putting the מנחה in to make it holy. Again the vessel seems to be sitting on the ground.

phrases.english: He said to him: He places it into this vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מנחה is placed into this vessel, which was on the ground

steps.title: Can a vessel on the ground sanctify
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן objects that a vessel resting on the ground cannot sanctify a מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does one sanctify in a vessel that is on the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges this answer just as he challenged the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly רבי ירמיה's question from step 11: does a vessel on the ground sanctify? רב נחמן assumes it does not.

phrases.english: But does one sanctify
in a vessel that is on the ground?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מְקַדְּשִׁין בִּכְלִי שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי קַרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: Sanctifying a מנחה in a vessel on the ground
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vessel on the ground seems unable to sanctify

steps.title: Again, a כהן lifts the vessel
steps.stepSummary: אבימי gives the same answer: another כהן lifts the vessel first.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A כהן lifts it.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי avoids the question again by saying the vessel is held up by a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once more אבימי does not rule on a vessel resting on the ground. This is why the question stays open, as רבי זירא said in step 12.

phrases.english: He said to him: That a priest lifts it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23, repeating the answer of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the case: the vessel is lifted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מנחה is put into a vessel resting on the ground
steps.terutzMaskana: Another כהן holds the vessel up

steps.title: Then you need three כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן points out that this approach would need three כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, you have made it need three כהנים!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן attacks אבימי's repeated answer. It makes the service need too many כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this approach, one כהן holds the vessel, one puts the מנחה in, and one takes the קומץ. רב נחמן finds that too complicated to be correct.

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
you have required three priests!
phrases.notes: One to hold the vessel, one to put the מנחה in, and one to take the קומץ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answers of steps 20 and 24
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that a כהן lifts the vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes the service need three כהנים, which seems unreasonable

steps.title: Even thirteen is fine, like the daily offering
steps.stepSummary: אבימי answers that the service could even need thirteen כהנים, as the תמיד does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Let it need thirteen, like the תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי rejects the challenge. Needing many כהנים is not a problem, because the תמיד already uses thirteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is already a known example of a service split among many כהנים, so three is not strange. אבימי keeps his answer, and the question about a vessel on the ground stays unanswered.
steps.whatToRemember: אבימי always avoided the question by saying a כהן lifts the vessel, so it never sat on the ground. That is why his story does not settle the question of a vessel on the ground. The question is put to רב ששת in step 29.

phrases.english: He said to him: And let it require
thirteen, like the daily offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precedent: the תמיד uses many כהנים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Needing three כהנים is too much
steps.terutzMaskana: Many כהנים are no problem, just as the תמיד uses thirteen

steps.title: The משנה lists the services of a מנחה but never mentions lifting
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן cites a משנה that lists the services of a מנחה where a wrong intention matters. Lifting the vessel off the ground is not on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: 'This is the rule: anyone who takes the handful, puts it in a vessel, carries it, or burns it, intending to eat something normally eaten (outside its proper place), etc.' But lifting the vessel is not listed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן brings a משנה to challenge אבימי's idea that a second כהן lifts the vessel off the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists every key service of a מנחה where a wrong intention can make it פסול. If lifting the vessel were a needed part of the service, it should be on that list. Since it is missing, it seems lifting is not needed, so אבימי's setup looks wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who takes the handful (קמיצה) from the מנחה
The one who carries the קומץ to the מזבח
The one who burns the קומץ on the מזבח
Lifts (here, lifting the vessel off the ground)

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
This is the rule:
anyone who takes the handful, or puts it in a vessel,
or carries it, or burns it,
intending to eat something that is normally eaten, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on to say this is about a wrong intention to eat or burn it outside its proper place.

phrases.english: Yet lifting is not taught?
phrases.notes: This is the lifting אבימי described back in step 24, where another כהן picks the vessel up off the floor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אבימי accepted that even many כהנים could be needed, רב נחמן attacks from a משנה that leaves out lifting.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבימי's claim that another כהן lifts the vessel off the ground
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists all the key services of a מנחה. Lifting is missing, so it should not be a required step.

steps.title: The משנה lists services, not the number of כהנים
steps.stepSummary: אבימי answers that the משנה only lists the services themselves, not every כהן who takes part.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא listed the order of the services, not the order of the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: אבימי defends himself. The משנה was not trying to describe everyone who helps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists the services where a wrong intention counts: קמיצה, putting into the vessel, carrying and burning. Lifting the vessel is just a helper's job so that the vessel is held in a hand. It is not one of those services, so leaving it out proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The author or teacher of the משנה
The order or list of כהנים involved

phrases.english: The תנא listed the order of the services,
and not the order of the כהנים.

steps.whatToRemember: אבימי holds firm: a vessel on the ground can work if another כהן lifts it. The משנה's list does not argue against this, because it counts services, not helpers.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists everything done in a מנחה, so lifting should have been there.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only the actual services, not each כהן's helping role.

steps.title: May one take the קמיצה from a vessel resting on the ground?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת is asked whether קמיצה may be done from a vessel that sits on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רב ששת: What is the law about taking a handful from a vessel that is resting on the ground?
steps.whatsHappening: The same open question, whether one may take a קומץ from a vessel resting on the ground, is now asked of רב ששת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question רבי ירמיה raised in step 11 and רב נחמן pressed on אבימי in step 19. אבימי avoided it by having a כהן lift the vessel. Now the question is put directly to רב ששת: is קמיצה valid when the מנחה sits in a vessel resting on the ground?

phrases.english: They asked רב ששת:
What is the law about taking a handful
from a vessel resting on the ground?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the same unresolved question from steps 11 and 19, taking a קומץ from a vessel on the ground, to רב ששת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is קמיצה valid when done from a vessel resting on the ground?

steps.title: רב ששת points to how the לחם הפנים and בזיכין are handled
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells them to look at what is done in the היכל when the לחם הפנים and its bowls of לבונה are changed each שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Go out and see what they do inside. Four כהנים enter: two hold the two rows of bread and two hold the two bowls of לבונה. Four more go in ahead of them: two to take away the two old rows and two to take away the two old bowls.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers by pointing to a משנה about changing the לחם הפנים on שבת. This step sets out the case. The גמרא will next show how it answers the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes how the bread and the בזיכין are taken off the שולחן. The old bowls are lifted from where they rest, and their לבונה is later burned. רב ששת brings this practice as the model for the case of a vessel resting in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Arrangements, the two rows of לחם הפנים
Bowls holding the לבונה that sit with the לחם הפנים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't expect the full proof yet. Here רב ששת only quotes how the bread and bowls are changed. How this answers the question comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Go out and see what they do inside.
phrases.notes: Inside means in the היכל, where the שולחן with the לחם הפנים stands.

phrases.english: Four כהנים enter,
two holding the two rows of bread,
and two holding the two bowls,
and four go in ahead of them,
two to take away the two rows,
and two to take away the two bowls.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 29 by pointing to practice in the בית המקדש.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב ששת points to the משנה about removing the לחם הפנים and בזיכין as the model for the answer. The details come next.
